newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS- Private placements predominate.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS- Private placements predominate.

text.p: Hong Kong dollar private placements were prominent in a quiet Asian debt market on Friday.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Societe Generale Asia privately placed a HK$600 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue for Shanghai Commercial Bank.

The issue matures in five years but can be put or called after three. It pays a margin of 35 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 40.5 basis points.
A HK$200 million six-month floating rate certificates of deposit issue was privately placed for Dao Heng Bank by arranger Jardine Fleming Bank.
The certificates were issued at par to float at 10 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
In other news, Indian utility Calcutta Electricity Supply Corp (CESC) plans to issue a seven-year dollar-denominated floating rate note issue, lead manager ANZ Investment bank said.
ANZ said the deal is likely to be launched in April.

South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy said that the country's financial institutions borrowed US$2.68 billion in the first quarter of 1997 by issuing overseas bonds with more than five years maturity.
Korea Development Bank issued a total of US$1.15 billion worth of bonds during the period, the Korea Export-Import Bank of Korea, US$1.45 billion, and Hanil Bank, US$80 million.
The finance ministry's statement said interest rates on short-term borrowings rose slightly as Japanese banks reduced liquidity supply.
But Korean financial institutions faced no problem as the central bank had released liquidity from its foreign currency reserves, it said.
